activities.anchor: The founding problem was named by Woodrow Wilson
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a dichotomy briefing
activities.name: adminDichSpot

config.prompt: One line of this student's briefing on Wilson is wrong — click it:
lines: Wilson's 1887 essay asked how government can be run competently without corrupting democracy.
The politics–administration dichotomy: elected politicians decide what to do, neutral professionals decide how.
Since every 'how' is also a 'what', the dichotomy has survived contact with reality fully intact.
Even so, the question the dichotomy framed still organises the field.
config.correction: The dichotomy has never survived contact with reality intact — every 'how' is also a 'what'.
config.why: But the question it framed — steer competence without smothering it, and vice versa — still organises the field.

activities.anchor: in the patterns of their daily coping
activities.caption: walk a caseworker's afternoon of discretion
activities.name: adminStreetBranch

config.root: A street-level caseworker faces more clients than time — Lipsky's street-level bureaucrats. Whatever coping pattern she settles into becomes, in effect, policy.

start.text: The afternoon queue exceeds the hours. Which claims get expedited?

choices.label: Whichever she judges most urgent
choices.feedback: Personal judgement is now doing the work the statute's categories were meant to do.

choices.label: Whichever files are complete and easy to close
choices.feedback: Processing ease, not need, now sets the pace of the office.

gap.text: The statute never told her to do either — the gap between rule and case is hers to fill. Next choice: which cases can wait?

choices.label: The ambiguous ones, until they clarify
choices.feedback: Ambiguity now carries a price in waiting time.

choices.label: The claimants who return angry every week
choices.feedback: The office now rewards docility — a policy nobody voted on.

pattern.text: By year's end the pattern is settled: some claim types move fast, others stall in the queue.

config.why: Lipsky's finding: with more clients than time, frontline workers effectively make policy as they cope — which claims get expedited, which infractions ignored, which students pushed. Governance happens at the desk, not only in the chamber.

activities.anchor: Day to day, an agency exercises power in three forms
activities.caption: file each action under its hat
activities.name: adminHatsSort

config.prompt: One institution, three hats — file each agency action:

items.label: writing the precise emission limit behind a clean-air act
filling in a statute with regulations that carry the force of law
examining tax returns at random, with no suspicion of wrongdoing
a trial-like hearing before an administrative law judge
deciding whether a rule was broken and what the penalty is

config.why: The hats mirror the three branches of government. Note the enforcement oddity: unlike police, agencies generally do not need suspicion of wrongdoing to act.

activities.name: adminLawCloze

config.text: Legislatures cannot keep up with the detail modern life needs, so they delegate: agencies produce %%0%% — regulations with real legal force, enforceable in the courts, valid only within the %%1%% of the authority the legislature handed over.
config.hint: The name of the legal output, and the limit that keeps every agency power traceable to a statute.

activities.caption: call the span from spoils to sunshine
activities.name: adminFoiaEst

config.prompt: Roughly how many years separate the Pendleton Act (1883) from the Freedom of Information Act (1966)?
config.why: 83 years: merit appointments arrive in 1883; the citizen's direct tool for demanding the records arrives in 1966. Unless one of a short list of exceptions applies — national security, personal privacy, trade secrets — the government must disclose.

activities.anchor: None of these checks is sufficient alone
activities.caption: pair each watcher with the failure it catches
activities.name: adminWatchMatch

config.prompt: The accountability layers — pair each watcher with its catch:
config.why: Each catches a different failure; layered together they are the legitimacy engine of unelected power — the administrative state is defensible exactly to the degree that the layering works.

activities.caption: drag the divider — subsidiarity versus uniformity
activities.name: adminFedCompare

config.prompt: The two principles that justify splitting the work — drag the divider.

before.label: Subsidiarity
before.text: Decisions at the lowest level competent to make them: local knowledge is real knowledge, and local accountability is the sharpest.

after.label: Uniformity
after.text: Some goods — rights, environmental floors, a single market — must not vary by postcode, so the top level must set the floor.

config.why: The tension between the two is where most federal politics happens; the craft of the field is managing the trade-off, not picking a side.
